content: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard language used to create and structure webpages. HTML documents contain elements represented by tags. Common elements include headings, paragraphs, images, links, buttons, tables, forms and containers.

CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. CSS controls the visual appearance of websites. It can change colors, fonts, backgrounds, spacing, borders, positioning, animations and layouts. CSS can be written inline, inside style elements or in external stylesheets.

JavaScript is a programming language used to create interactive websites and applications. It can modify webpage content, respond to user actions, calculate values, communicate with servers and process information. JavaScript runs in browsers and can also run on servers using environments such as Node.js.

Python is a general-purpose programming language known for its readable syntax. It is commonly used for automation, artificial intelligence, scientific computing, data processing, web development and scripting. Python uses indentation to define code blocks.

JSON stands for JavaScript Object Notation. It is a lightweight data format used to store and exchange structured information. JSON supports strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects and null values. JSON is commonly used by APIs and configuration files.

An API is an application programming interface. It allows different software applications to communicate with each other. APIs commonly receive requests and return responses. HTTP APIs often use methods such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
HTTP is a communication protocol used by web browsers and servers. HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP and uses encryption through TLS to protect information during transmission.

A web browser is software used to access websites and web applications. Browsers interpret HTML, CSS and JavaScript and display the resulting interface. Examples include Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Edge.

A server is a computer or software system that provides services or resources to other computers. Web servers receive requests and return responses. Servers can process information, store files, authenticate users and run applications.

A database is an organized collection of information that can be stored, searched, updated and managed. Relational databases organize information into tables, while document databases can store flexible structured records.

Cloudflare Workers is a serverless platform that allows developers to execute code on Cloudflare infrastructure. Workers can receive HTTP requests, process data, communicate with APIs and connect to storage services.

GitHub is a platform for hosting Git repositories. Developers use it to store source code, track changes, collaborate on projects and publish software. A repository can contain HTML, JavaScript, Python, JSON, images and documentation.
Git is a version control system used to track changes in files. It allows developers to create commits, branches and merges. Git helps developers manage different versions of a project.

A variable is a named storage location used by a program to hold information. In JavaScript, let and const are commonly used to declare variables. Variables can contain strings, numbers, objects, arrays and other values.
A function is a reusable block of programming instructions. Functions can receive parameters, perform operations and return results. They help organize programs into smaller manageable sections.

An array is a data structure that stores multiple values in an ordered collection. JavaScript arrays can contain strings, numbers, objects and other arrays. Array methods include map, filter, find, push and pop.
An object is a data structure that stores information as key-value pairs. Objects are commonly used to represent users, settings, products and other structured information.
A loop repeats a section of code. Common JavaScript loops include for, while and for...of. Loops are useful when processing arrays, repeating calculations or performing tasks multiple times.
An if statement allows a program to make decisions based on conditions. If the condition is true, one section of code runs. Else and else if can be used to handle alternative conditions.

Machine learning is a field of artificial intelligence where computer systems learn patterns from data. Machine learning models can make predictions, classify information and identify relationships in datasets.

Artificial intelligence refers to computer systems designed to perform tasks associated with human intelligence. These tasks include understanding language, recognizing patterns, generating content and solving problems.

A large language model is an artificial intelligence model trained on large amounts of text. It learns statistical patterns in language and uses them to generate responses, summarize information and assist with programming.
A chatbot is a software application that communicates with users through text or voice. Chatbots can use predefined responses, search databases, connect to APIs or use artificial intelligence models.
A dataset is a collection of information used for analysis, searching or machine learning. Datasets can contain text, numbers, images, audio, video or structured records.
Training data is information used to teach a machine learning model. The quality, diversity and accuracy of training data can influence the behavior and performance of the resulting model.
A search engine retrieves information based on a user's query. Search systems can use keywords, indexing, ranking algorithms and semantic similarity to find relevant results.
A text tokenizer divides text into smaller units called tokens. Depending on the tokenizer, tokens can represent words, parts of words, punctuation or individual characters.
A programming language is a formal language used to write instructions for computers. Examples include Python, JavaScript, Java, C, C++, C#, Rust and Go.
An algorithm is a sequence of instructions designed to solve a problem or perform a calculation. Algorithms are used in sorting, searching, encryption, data processing and artificial intelligence.
A computer processor, also called a CPU, executes instructions and performs calculations. CPUs are important components in computers, servers, smartphones and other electronic devices.

RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It provides temporary storage for information that a computer is actively using. RAM is generally faster than long-term storage but loses its contents when power is removed.
An operating system manages computer hardware and software resources. Examples include Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS.

A file extension identifies the general format of a file. Examples include .html for HTML documents, .css for stylesheets, .js for JavaScript, .json for JSON data, .py for Python and .txt for plain text.
A local file is stored directly on a device. A remote file is stored on another computer or server and accessed through a network or internet connection.
A frontend is the part of an application that users interact with. It commonly includes the interface, buttons, menus, forms and visual elements.
A backend handles application logic, data processing, authentication and communication with databases or other services. Users usually interact with the backend through an API.
A full-stack application contains both frontend and backend components. These components work together to provide a complete software experience.
Responsive web design allows a website to adapt to different screen sizes. CSS media queries, flexible layouts and relative sizing help websites work on phones, tablets and desktop computers.
An event listener waits for a specific event and executes a function when that event occurs. JavaScript can listen for clicks, keyboard input, form submissions and other browser events.
The Document Object Model, commonly called the DOM, represents an HTML document as a tree of objects. JavaScript can use the DOM to read, create, modify and remove webpage elements.
The fetch function in JavaScript sends network requests and returns a Promise. It is commonly used to communicate with APIs and retrieve information from remote servers.
A Promise represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation. JavaScript uses promises for operations such as network requests, file processing and timers.
Async and await provide syntax for working with asynchronous JavaScript operations. They make promise-based code easier to read and organize.
Local storage is a browser feature that allows websites to save small amounts of information on a device. Stored values generally remain available after the browser is closed.
An authentication system verifies the identity of a user. Applications commonly use passwords, secure tokens, passkeys or other verification methods.
Encryption transforms information into a protected format that requires an appropriate key to read. Encryption helps protect sensitive information during storage and communication.
A URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. It identifies the location of a resource on the internet. URLs can contain a protocol, domain, path, query parameters and fragment identifier.
A domain name is a human-readable address used to locate internet resources. Domain names are translated into IP addresses through the Domain Name System, known as DNS.
An IP address identifies a device or network interface on an IP network. IPv4 and IPv6 are two versions of the Internet Protocol.
A web application is software accessed through a web browser. Web applications can provide services such as messaging, document editing, online shopping, games and collaboration.
A software library is reusable code that developers can include in their projects. Libraries provide existing functions and components that reduce the amount of code developers need to write.
An open-source project makes its source code available under a license that defines how others can use, modify and distribute it.
Debugging is the process of identifying, understanding and correcting errors in software. Developers commonly use console messages, logs, breakpoints and testing tools to debug programs.
A syntax error occurs when code does not follow the grammatical rules of its programming language. Syntax errors can prevent a program from running correctly.
A runtime error occurs while a program is executing. Runtime errors can result from invalid operations, missing resources, unexpected data or other execution problems.
A software update introduces changes to an application. Updates can include new features, performance improvements, bug fixes and security improvements.
A cache stores copies of previously accessed information to make future requests faster. Browsers, servers and applications commonly use caching to improve performance.
A content delivery network is a distributed network of servers that delivers content from locations closer to users. CDNs can improve loading speeds and reduce pressure on origin servers.
A cloud computing service provides computing resources over the internet. Cloud services can offer servers, databases, storage, networking and application hosting.
Object storage is a storage system designed to store files as objects. It is commonly used for images, videos, backups, documents and other large files.
A relational database stores information in tables containing rows and columns. SQL is commonly used to create, retrieve, update and delete relational database records.
A primary key uniquely identifies a record in a database table. A foreign key establishes a relationship between records in different tables.
A backup is a separate copy of information that can be used to restore data after accidental deletion, corruption or hardware failure.
A software framework provides a structure and set of tools for building applications. Frameworks often define conventions and provide reusable components.
Version control helps developers track the history of changes in a project. It makes collaboration easier and allows earlier versions of files to be recovered.
A command-line interface allows users to interact with a computer by entering text commands. Developers use command-line tools to manage files, execute programs and operate development environments.
A compiler translates source code into another representation, such as machine code. An interpreter executes program instructions through an execution environment.
An HTML element usually consists of an opening tag, content and a closing tag. Some elements, such as img and input, do not use a separate closing tag.
CSS Flexbox is a layout system designed to arrange elements along a row or column. It provides controls for alignment, spacing, wrapping and flexible sizing.
CSS Grid is a layout system that allows developers to arrange webpage elements in rows and columns. It is useful for complex two-dimensional layouts.
A regular expression is a pattern used to search, match or replace text. Regular expressions are supported by many programming languages and text-processing tools.
A CSV file stands for Comma-Separated Values. It stores tabular information as plain text, with values separated by delimiters, commonly commas.
Markdown is a lightweight markup language used to format text. It supports headings, lists, links, images, code blocks and emphasis.
A software license defines the permissions and restrictions associated with using, modifying and distributing software.

An application programming interface can expose specific operations while hiding the internal implementation of a service. This allows different systems to communicate without sharing all their internal code.
A network protocol defines rules for exchanging information between devices. Examples include HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, UDP, DNS and WebSocket.
WebSockets provide a persistent communication connection between a client and a server. They are useful for real-time applications such as multiplayer games and chat systems.
A multiplayer game allows multiple players to participate in the same game environment. Multiplayer systems may use servers to synchronize player positions, actions and game state.
A three-dimensional computer graphics scene can contain objects, lights, cameras, materials and textures. WebGL and WebGPU allow browsers to render interactive graphics.
Three.js is a JavaScript library used to create and display three-dimensional graphics in web browsers. It provides tools for scenes, cameras, geometry, lighting, materials and animation.
An image file stores visual information. Common formats include PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG. Different formats offer different compression, animation and transparency capabilities.
An SVG file stores vector graphics using XML-based markup. SVG images can scale without losing sharpness and can be styled using CSS.
Audio files store sound information. Common audio formats include MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC and OGG.
A video file contains moving visual information and may include audio, subtitles and metadata. Common formats include MP4, WebM and MOV.

Data compression reduces the amount of storage space required by information. Lossless compression preserves the original data, while lossy compression removes some information to achieve smaller files.
A checksum is a value calculated from data and can help detect accidental changes or corruption. Cryptographic hash functions provide stronger properties for verifying data integrity.
A software dependency is an external package, library or service that an application relies on to function.
An environment variable is a configuration value provided to a running program through its environment. It is often used for deployment settings and backend secrets.
A public repository allows people to view its files and source code. Private repositories restrict access to authorized users.
A GitHub raw URL provides direct access to the contents of a file stored in a repository. Raw URLs can be used to retrieve public text files and scripts.
A static website serves files such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images without requiring server-side processing for every page request.

An HTTP status code communicates the result of a request. Common codes include 200 for success, 301 for redirection, 400 for a bad request, 403 for forbidden access, 404 for not found and 500 for an internal server error.
The purpose of software testing is to check whether an application behaves as expected. Testing can be performed manually or automatically using test scripts.
A user interface is the part of a software application through which a person interacts with its functionality. Good interfaces aim to make actions understandable and easy to perform.
